key_insight: Telescopic Language Models train a single Transformer to work across a range of compute budgets by nesting smaller-capacity submodels inside a full-capacity model. This lets one deployed model behave like a whole family of models, instead of requiring separate training runs for each budget.
problem_solved: Serving different latency, memory, or compute budgets usually requires training or compressing multiple separate models. This paper addresses the inefficiency of maintaining many models by creating one model that can reliably adapt to multiple capacity levels.
method: Train a nested-capacity Transformer with stochastic prefix supervision, so a randomly chosen truncated prefix of the capacity axis learns from the full next-token target.
Include a full-capacity anchor pass at every step to preserve the performance of the largest model while also teaching smaller prefixes.
Produce a single deployed artifact that can be used as a continuum of valid language models across compute budgets.
impact: For practitioners, TLM could simplify deployment by reducing the need for multiple separately tuned models. It offers a practical path to serving different inference budgets with one shared model and one training pipeline.
